title: Compare archival, documentary and literary representations

questions.prompt: Fictional Francophone migration archive: which document is most likely a primary source for a particular departure?
choices: A contemporary witness's dated letter.
A modern novel inspired by the event.
A recent textbook overview.
questions.explanation: A firsthand letter created at the time can be primary evidence for the writer's account.

questions.prompt: Identity and migration literature: which comparison distinguishes fictionalized exile from a person's documented recollections?
choices: Fiction and testimony always have identical evidentiary status.
Every novel is a verbatim transcript.
A novel may reconstruct imagined experience, while testimony records a person's account.
questions.explanation: Genres differ in their claims to direct evidence and reconstruction.

questions.prompt: A migration documentary uses actors to stage a family's departure. Which French description labels the reconstruction responsibly?
choices: Un témoignage spontané joué par des acteurs.
Une reconstitution fondée sur des sources identifiées.
Une archive filmée directement lors d'un événement non enregistré.
questions.explanation: Reconstitution identifies staging rather than an original recording.

questions.prompt: Citing a fictional migrant's dated archival letter: what contextual and provenance details should accompany the quotation?
choices: Author, date, archive reference and relevant context.
Only a decorative illustration.
A guarantee that the author represented everyone.
questions.explanation: Provenance and context allow the quotation to be assessed.

questions.prompt: Reading a novel about intergenerational migration memory: choose a balanced interpretation of the narrator's relationship to the author.
choices: Le narrateur et l'auteur sont toujours la même personne.
Toute fiction est un document officiel.
Le narrateur présente une mémoire fragmentaire, qui ne se confond pas nécessairement avec celle de l'auteur.
questions.explanation: Narrator and author are distinct analytical roles unless evidence says otherwise.

questions.prompt: A migration-family manuscript has disputed authorship. Which French phrase accurately signals uncertainty about its attribution?
choices: L'attribution ne nécessite jamais de justification.
Ce manuscrit serait attribuable à une autrice encore débattue.
L'autrice est certainement identifiée sans indice.
questions.explanation: Conditional phrasing conveys an attribution still under examination.

questions.prompt: Comparing a migration documentary with a contemporary administrative record: which formal French sentence respects their different genres?
choices: Le film dramatise la scène que l'archive décrit sobrement.
Le film prouve que l'archive est sans valeur.
Les deux supports sont nécessairement identiques.
questions.explanation: Dramatization and description can present one event differently without invalidating either.

questions.prompt: An archival letter about exile is abridged for an exhibit. What editorial practice transparently reports omitted text?
choices: Hide omissions and call the excerpt complete.
Replace missing sentences with invented quotations.
Mark omitted passages and explain selection criteria.
questions.explanation: An explicit abridgment disclosure keeps selection decisions visible.

questions.prompt: Comparing two cultural depictions of belonging after migration: choose a responsible, nonuniversalizing interpretive thesis.
choices: Aucune perspective ne peut être contestée.
Les deux œuvres donnent des perspectives différentes sur la mémoire familiale.
Les œuvres prouvent une seule mémoire universelle.
questions.explanation: The bounded thesis compares representations without universalizing them.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le registre note des départs, mais pas les raisons individuelles. » What is missing?
choices: The travelers' stated personal motives.
The fact that departures were recorded.
The existence of the register.
questions.explanation: An administrative record of departures need not document why each person left.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le film intègre un journal intime lu par une comédienne. » What should viewers distinguish?
choices: The actor as necessarily the diary's author.
The reading as an unedited original voice recording.
The diary text from the performance of its reading.
questions.explanation: An actor's performance is a mediation of the written source.

questions.prompt: Read: « L'écrivain transforme un quartier réel en lieu symbolique. » Which reading is careful?
choices: The neighborhood cannot exist historically.
The literary setting may evoke reality without reproducing every fact.
Every plot event happened exactly as narrated.
questions.explanation: Literary symbolism should not be confused with documentary precision.

questions.prompt: Read: « La photographie est datée de 1930, mais sa légende date de 1980. » What is the source distinction?
choices: The image and its caption were produced in different periods.
The caption was written before the photograph.
The photograph cannot be used for study.
questions.explanation: A later caption can reflect retrospective framing.

questions.prompt: Read: « L'archive conserve surtout des voix administratives. » Which perspective may be underrepresented?
choices: The administrators whose reports survive.
Every official whose documents are held.
People discussed by officials but not heard directly.
questions.explanation: Institutional selection can leave community perspectives underdocumented.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le personnage affirme se souvenir parfaitement de son enfance. » Which literary question is relevant?
choices: Does a claim to memory prove the novel is nonfiction?
Is the narrator reliable in the text's narrative design?
Does the character therefore speak for every child?
questions.explanation: Literary analysis examines narrative reliability, not just asserted certainty.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le sous-titrage ne rend pas le jeu de mots du dialogue original. » What may be lost?
choices: Humor and layered meanings carried by language.
The video's publication date.
Whether any actors appear.
questions.explanation: Wordplay can be difficult to carry across languages in subtitles.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le documentaire juxtapose deux témoignages contradictoires. » What follows?
choices: One witness is automatically lying.
All testimony must be discarded.
The viewer should compare viewpoints and supporting details.
questions.explanation: Contradiction warrants analysis rather than an automatic verdict.

questions.prompt: Read: « Une chanson évoque l'exil par des images poétiques. » How should it be approached?
choices: As an exact transcript of every migrant's story.
As an artistic representation that may carry cultural memory.
As a literal immigration database.
questions.explanation: Poetic imagery communicates experience without being a population register.

questions.prompt: You must cite a novel's account of an historical event. Which qualification fits?
choices: Présenter la scène comme une représentation littéraire, à comparer avec les archives.
Présenter tous les dialogues inventés comme des citations historiques.
Supprimer la distinction entre fiction et archive.
questions.explanation: Fiction can illuminate perspectives but requires a clear evidentiary boundary.

questions.prompt: A museum label uses a later photograph to illustrate an earlier event. What should it disclose?
choices: The image was captured during the earlier event.
Photographs have no dates worth reporting.
The image is illustrative and was taken after the event.
questions.explanation: Chronological disclosure prevents misleading viewers about direct evidence.

questions.prompt: Two archives use different names for the same community. Which strategy is most responsible?
choices: Erase all terms without explaining the sources.
Explain historical terminology and consult community self-descriptions.
Assume official labels never change.
questions.explanation: Naming practices carry historical power and require context.

questions.prompt: You are analyzing a film that recreates a courtroom speech. What should you verify?
choices: Whether a contemporaneous transcript supports the dialogue.
Whether the actor has a convincing accent only.
Whether the scene has dramatic lighting.
questions.explanation: A cinematic reconstruction must not be mistaken for a verbatim record.

questions.prompt: A literary narrator uses « nous » without specifying the group. What question matters?
choices: Whether every reader is necessarily addressed.
Whether plural pronouns have no rhetorical effect.
Who is included or excluded by the collective voice?
questions.explanation: The scope of nous shapes collective identity and representation.

questions.prompt: A text was translated from another language. What is a sound comparison method?
choices: Assume translation erases the source culture.
Identify shifts in register, connotation and omitted context.
Treat every translation as mechanically identical.
questions.explanation: Translation can shift meaning, so comparing with the original is useful.

questions.prompt: A documentary uses archival audio over unrelated images. What should a reviewer ask?
choices: Whether the montage implies a connection not documented by the source.
Whether every photograph must have sound.
Whether audio alone proves the images' provenance.
questions.explanation: Editing can suggest relationships the original sources do not establish.

questions.prompt: A family history includes conflicting memories of a journey. Which presentation is ethical?
choices: Blend them into one fabricated unanimous quotation.
Delete disagreements without disclosure.
Attribute each account and acknowledge the unresolved differences.
questions.explanation: Attribution and transparency preserve divergent testimony.

questions.prompt: Your conclusion compares an archive, film and poem about migration. Which is strongest?
choices: Le poème invalide automatiquement toute archive.
L'archive documente des faits administratifs, tandis que le film et le poème proposent d'autres mises en récit.
Les trois œuvres prouvent chaque détail historique à l'identique.
questions.explanation: Synthesis distinguishes evidence types and artistic narratives without collapsing them.
